artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for sparse-literature detection and Stage 4a reconciliation

next_steps: Task complete; all 7 phases implemented and verified. No further action required unless the literature extension is redeployed, in which case test-lit-pipeline.sh should be re-run against the deployed .claude/ tree.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added sparse-coverage detection (LITERATURE_SPARSE_THRESHOLD, machine-readable lit-coverage marker, SPARSE_PROMPT_NEEDED directive) to literature-briefing.sh and literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh, and reconciled the drifted Stage 4a flow across all six --lit skills into one shared core-context block that calls the resolver, branches on all six directives, offers a new "Search online to ingest" option wired to the literature-ingest-online.sh bridge, and fixes the orchestrator_mode autonomy contract so /orchestrate --lit never prompts in any phase.

memory_candidates.content: When extracting N near-duplicate skill blocks into one shared context file to eliminate a drift class, place the shared file in the DEPLOYMENT-UNCONDITIONAL layer (e.g. core context) rather than the domain extension's own context, even if the content is domain-specific -- otherwise the @-import silently breaks whenever the domain extension is deselected. Document the reasoning inline in the shared file's header so future edits do not move it back.

When a delegation-context boolean flag (e.g. orchestrator_mode) is reused for a SECOND, unrelated gating purpose beyond its original meaning, add an explicit dual-consumer cross-reference note at both consumer sites (not just one) -- a future edit to either consumer's semantics needs to see the other consumer to avoid silently regressing it.

The no-task-references-in-deliverables rule is easy to violate accidentally when writing skill/doc prose that names a dependency bridge or prior task's deliverable by habit (e.g. "the task-866 bridge"). Grep the full diff for task-number patterns (grep -rniE 'task[ -]?[0-9]{2,4}\b') across every file touched outside specs/** as a final pre-commit check, not just the files you remember editing.
